note: From the OpenStreetMap export (11 October 2026), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks: two short side platforms on the Hazel Grove line (about 80 m: trains stop 20 m south of the station's point, so a two-car unit stands on them as they are and a four-car one once they're extended; a six-car one stands off the north end, as at a real short platform, which `longest` says), 2.1 m outside its two tracks, with steps up to Moorland Road over the line at the north end, which is where passengers come and go; the Brethren's meeting room stands to the west. Positive v is east. Photos (geograph 4788246, 4788716, 4788706, 4788240 and 4788764 Gerald England 2016, 4252865 Nigel Thompson 2010, 3337870 Peter Barr 2013, 1705461 and 1705392 2010, 2571121 David Dixon 2011): no lifts and no steps down to the platforms: from Moorland Road each platform has a long ramp along the line, the west one outside the platform fence (with dog-leg steps by the road too), the east one on from the platform's north end along the cutting; drawn as one ramp each from the platform's north end up to the road (the way across). The lifts are the game's, standing behind the cutting walls by the bridge. One Northern-blue shelter a platform: a short apex-roofed one 20-30 m from the west platform's north end, a longer flat-roofed one about 10 m from the east one's (both drawn as the usual glass shelter); no canopy at the real station, so the canopy is the game's. Tall pale lamp columns. No ticket machine, cycle stands or car park in the photos. A departure board on each platform.
